column1: # docs/provenance/REPLAY-MANIFEST.tsv — for `docs/ledger-tools/provenance_replay.py`.
# ⚠️ THIS IS NOT `MANIFEST.tsv`, AND THE TWO ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS.
#   MANIFEST.tsv  + verify.sh   (math)  — "are the bundle's files unaltered, and
#                                         does the program still match the blob
#                                         we pinned?"   Pins the CURRENT artifact.
#   REPLAY-MANIFEST.tsv         (this)  — "do the executor's logged tool calls
#                                         still REPRODUCE the artifact as born?"
#                                         Pins the artifact AS BORN, by BLOB CONTENT.
# Both are wanted. Neither subsumes the other: a file can be byte-identical to a
# pin that was itself re-pinned after an edit, which is exactly the state S2
# bundle <TAB> target (absolute path AS THE EXECUTOR SAW IT) <TAB> git rev:path OR blob id <TAB> source (optional)
#   python3 docs/ledger-tools/provenance_replay.py --manifest docs/provenance/REPLAY-MANIFEST.tsv
# ⛔ THE REV IS PINNED TO THE BIRTH COMMIT, AND MY FIRST VERSION OF THIS FILE HAD
# IT WRONG. At 13:2x I wrote "`--against HEAD:…` is deliberate, not a pin — a
# pinned rev would pass forever while the artifact drifted." That reasoning is
# right for a FROZEN artifact and wrong for a LIVE MODULE. At 14:0x math added
# 841 lines of S3(b) to `Program.lean`; the drift was legitimate development, and
# HEAD-anchoring turned a birth record into a permanent RED. A gate that goes red
# for expected behaviour is a gate someone switches off.
# A birth record binds a BIRTH. Pinning `bf2de34` makes the replay claim -- "the
# executor's tool calls reproduce this file exactly" -- true and checkable
# forever. Drift of HEAD away from birth is normal and is verify.sh's question,
# not this one.
# ⛔⛔ RE-KEYED BY CONTENT, 2026-09-13 (desk row LP). THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS HISTORY, NOT THE LIVE PIN.
#   This row's third column read `bf2de34:SaltWorks/Stack/Program.lean` until today. The 2026-08-16
#   history purge REWROTE every sha, so `bf2de34` names no commit in public history, and a public
#   clone answers `invalid object name` (exit 2) before the transcript is even opened. The pin was
#   true when written and was orphaned, not wrong.
#   It now names the BLOB `b2bf183b`: a hash of the file's bytes, which no rewrite of history can change.
#   ⇒ Measured before re-keying, by a THIRD source: in two local object stores that predate the purge,
#     `bf2de34:SaltWorks/Stack/Program.lean` resolves to exactly `b2bf183b7b04290a…`. In public
#     history that blob is reachable from HEAD at the STACK-S2 commit, and this repository's own purge
#     map (docs/ledger-tools/flip-sha-map-0816.tsv) names that commit `5d62022` as `bf2de34`'s successor.
#     It is also the same blob
#     `verify.sh`'s `born` row (MANIFEST.tsv) matches by content. The two manifests now name ONE birth.
#   Driven with the private copy of the bundle (sha256 = WITHHELD.tsv's): the old row exits 2
#   (unresolvable rev); the re-keyed row replays 2 mutations to 24,070 bytes and 515 lines and exits
#   0 BOUND; the current pin `23bb06e7` in the same column exits 1 MISMATCH.
# ⛔⛔ A PUBLIC READER CAN NEVER RUN THIS REPLAY, AND THAT IS DECLARED HERE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED.
#   The bundle is WITHHELD (see WITHHELD.tsv: it carries strings this repository's own Scrub CI
#   refuses). In any public clone `provenance_replay.py --manifest` on this file exits 2,
#   COULD NOT CHECK, and says the bundle is declared withheld. **Exit 2 is not a pass, and it is not
#   a defect either: it is this hole, declared.** The replay is runnable ONLY by a holder of the
#   private copy, who can first prove the copy is the same bytes via the sha256 in WITHHELD.tsv.
#   What a public reader CAN run on this binding: `selftest.py` checks that every row here names an
#   object reachable from HEAD (the check that would have caught the purge), and `verify.sh`'s
#   `born` row checks the same blob by content.
# S2 — the bitonic sort. Born bf2de34 (pre-purge sha; blob b2bf183b); bundle a5d2ef7 (the next commit, also pre-purge).
